Looks like we've been making some strong plays! Let me quickly summarize our current game state and what's just happened.

1. We've played a **Humble Defector** and activated **Immaculate Magistrate** to put a +1/+1 counter on an **Elemental Token**.
2. We're in combat now, and I've declared **Etali, Primal Storm** and two Elemental Tokens as attackers.
3. We're still at a crucial point in the game, and our opponents are pressured!

Let's keep the momentum going. I'll call for priority to see our next options!

gameOver.message: Player GPT4om Rookie is the winner

annotations.description: In a 4-player Commander game, choosing yourself as the starting player means you go first but miss your first draw step. With Zurgo Helmsmasher as commander (an aggressive Mardu deck that wants to attack early), going first has some merit for tempo. However, in multiplayer Commander, going later is often advantageous because you get to draw an extra card and see what opponents are doing before committing. The conventional wisdom in 4-player games is that going last (or at least not first) is often better since you gain card advantage and political information. That said, going first with an aggressive commander like Zurgo can be defensible for early pressure, so this is debatable rather than a clear mistake.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose themselves (GPT4om Rookie) as the starting player
annotations.betterLine: In multiplayer Commander, choosing to go later (3rd or 4th) is generally advantageous for the extra draw and information. Could have chosen a different starting position, though going first with Zurgo aggro is at least arguable.

annotations.description: DSV3 Hist activated Elixir of Immortality on turn 2 with an empty graveyard, gaining 5 life but shuffling away the artifact for essentially no value. The Elixir's primary purpose is to recycle your graveyard back into your library, but with no cards in graveyard, the activation only gains 5 life at the cost of losing the artifact permanently (until drawn again). Additionally, they used colorless mana from Graven Cairns when they could have used it more efficiently, but the bigger issue is the pointless Elixir activation itself.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Elixir of Immortality on turn 2 with an empty graveyard, tapping both lands to pay {2} and gaining 5 life while shuffling the Elixir back into the library.
annotations.betterLine: Hold the Elixir of Immortality for later when there are meaningful cards in the graveyard to recycle. Instead, play the Mountain from hand and pass, setting up to cast Knight of the White Orchid on turn 3 (with WW from Caves of Koilos + another source) or develop the board in other ways.

annotations.description: Activating Myriad Landscape on turn 2 means sacrificing a land and paying 2 mana, leaving Kimi with no untapped lands this turn and getting two tapped Forests. While this ramps, it's premature — Kimi has two Forests in hand to play naturally over the next turns. The hand has Essence Warden (1 mana) and Swiftfoot Boots (2 mana) as early plays. By cracking Myriad Landscape now instead of playing a Forest from hand, Kimi loses tempo: they could have played Forest, then had 3 mana available (or 2 untapped + Myriad Landscape for future use). Playing a Forest from hand first and saving Myriad Landscape for a later turn when there are fewer land drops in hand would be more efficient, allowing earlier deployment of Essence Warden or Swiftfoot Boots.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Myriad Landscape's sacrifice ability on turn 2, using all available mana and sacrificing the land to fetch two tapped Forests.
annotations.betterLine: Play a Forest from hand, tap it and the existing Forest to cast Swiftfoot Boots (or hold up mana), saving Myriad Landscape for a later turn when natural land drops from hand are exhausted. This preserves tempo and allows earlier plays like Essence Warden on turn 3 with 3 lands available.

annotations.description: Knight of the White Orchid's ETB trigger will not activate because no opponent controls more lands than DSV3 Hist (who has 3 lands, tied with GPT4om's 3 and ahead of the others' 2). This wastes the card's primary value as a ramp spell. Waiting to deploy Knight when behind on lands would extract more value.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to cast Knight of the White Orchid when no opponent had more lands, making it a vanilla 2/2 first strike.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain from hand, cast Ajani, Caller of the Pride (building loyalty for future turns when creatures arrive), and save Knight of the White Orchid for a turn when an opponent has more lands to get the free Plains.

annotations.description: With 3 mana available on turn 3, casting Swiftfoot Boots (2 mana) leaves only 1 mana open with no creature to equip. Essence Warden (1 mana) is a strong early play in multiplayer that gains incremental life from every creature entering the battlefield, and playing it first would allow the remaining 2 mana to cast Swiftfoot Boots as well - getting both onto the battlefield this turn. Alternatively, playing Essence Warden + Elvish Skysweeper would develop the board with two creatures. Playing Boots alone with no creatures to protect is low-impact.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Swiftfoot Boots with 3 mana, leaving 1 mana unused and no creature on board to equip.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Essence Warden (1 mana) first, then cast Swiftfoot Boots (2 mana), deploying both permanents this turn. This develops the board and starts gaining life from opponents' creatures entering play.

annotations.description: Casting Masked Admirers (4 mana) before combat is suboptimal when holding Beastmaster Ascension. The Admirers could have been cast post-combat, and there's no particular reason to play it pre-combat since it doesn't have haste and won't affect combat this turn. More importantly, with only 4 mana available (3 Forests + Myriad Landscape), casting Masked Admirers uses all mana, preventing other plays like Elvish Skysweeper + Sylvan Safekeeper or Beastmaster Ascension (3 mana). Beastmaster Ascension at 3 mana would have been more impactful since Essence Warden could attack this turn to start accumulating quest counters, and it leaves 1 mana open for Sylvan Safekeeper or Elvish Skysweeper. The card draw from Admirers is nice but Beastmaster Ascension is a more powerful engine card that benefits from being deployed early.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Masked Admirers for 4 mana, using all available mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Beastmaster Ascension for 3 mana, then cast Sylvan Safekeeper or Elvish Skysweeper with remaining mana, and attack with Essence Warden to start building quest counters

annotations.description: Attacking DSV3 Hist with a 1/1 Essence Warden is essentially pointless - it deals only 1 damage and risks losing a valuable lifegain engine if DSV3 Hist has the 4/4 Knight of the White Orchid (with +1/+1 counters making it a 4/4) available to block, which would kill the Essence Warden. DSV3 Hist has a Knight of the White Orchid with two +1/+1 counters (4/4) that is tapped, so it can't block this turn. However, Essence Warden is more valuable as a lifegain engine in a multiplayer game than dealing 1 damage. Additionally, attacking into DSV3 Hist draws political attention when Kimi25 Story has a relatively modest board position. The Masked Admirers is summoning sick so can't attack, but sending a key utility creature into combat for 1 damage is questionable value.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked DSV3 Hist with Essence Warden (1/1) for 1 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Not attacking at all. Essence Warden is a valuable utility creature that gains life whenever any creature enters the battlefield. Risking it or drawing political attention for 1 damage is not worth it, even though the Knight is tapped this turn.

annotations.description: Kimi25 Story activated Myriad Landscape using all available mana without first casting a 1-mana creature. They had Sylvan Safekeeper (G) and Elvish Skysweeper (G) in hand, and could have cast one using 1 Forest, then still activated Myriad Landscape with the remaining 2 Forests + tapping Myriad Landscape. This would have developed the board further and triggered Essence Warden for 1 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Myriad Landscape immediately, using all 3 Forests for the {2} activation cost plus the sacrifice.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sylvan Safekeeper (or Elvish Skysweeper) for {G} first, gaining 1 life from Essence Warden, then activate Myriad Landscape with the remaining 2 Forests to search for 2 basic lands.

annotations.description: Played Oran-Rief, the Vastwood (enters tapped) instead of Gargoyle Castle (enters untapped), and then failed to cast a 1-drop creature (Elvish Skysweeper or Sylvan Safekeeper) with the untapped Forest. Playing Gargoyle Castle would have provided 2 mana: enough to cast a creature AND equip Swiftfoot Boots, significantly developing the board. Even with Oran-Rief, they should have cast a 1-drop with the untapped Forest.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Oran-Rief, the Vastwood (tapped) and passed without casting any spells, wasting 1 available green mana.
annotations.betterLine: Play Gargoyle Castle (untapped), cast Sylvan Safekeeper for G, then equip Swiftfoot Boots for 1 (colorless from Castle), giving Safekeeper hexproof and haste. This develops the board and protects a key utility creature.

annotations.description: Cycling Slippery Karst instead of playing it as a land is questionable. Kimi25 Story has 7 lands on the battlefield (3 tapped, 4 untapped) and expensive cards in hand like Siege Behemoth (7 mana) and Terastodon (8 mana). Playing Slippery Karst as a tapped land would accelerate toward casting these powerful threats. Cycling draws a random card but delays the mana development needed for the hand's payoffs. Additionally, cycling triggers Grok4 Johnny's Centaur Vinecrasher graveyard ability, potentially giving an opponent back a threat. The draw from cycling is unlikely to be better than the guaranteed mana acceleration toward Siege Behemoth or Terastodon.
annotations.actionTaken: Cycled Slippery Karst for {2} to draw a card instead of playing it as a land.
annotations.betterLine: Play Slippery Karst as a tapped land to reach 8 lands, enabling Terastodon next turn or Siege Behemoth this turn with the extra mana. This also avoids triggering Centaur Vinecrasher for the opponent.

annotations.description: Kimi25 Story is attacking GPT4om Rookie with a 1/1 Sylvan Safekeeper. While GPT4om Rookie has no blockers, the 1 damage is minimal. The choice of attack target is debatable - DSV3 Hist at 36 life has a Blood Artist (0/1) that could block but is more threatening long-term, while Grok4 Johnny at 37 life has no creatures to block. However, the real consideration is whether attacking with Sylvan Safekeeper is wise at all, since it's a valuable utility creature that provides shroud protection by sacrificing lands. Losing it in combat (if somehow blocked or removed) would be costly. That said, with no blockers available from GPT4om Rookie, the attack is safe. The 1 damage is nearly meaningless though, and the Beastmaster Ascension quest counter is the real value. With only 1 creature attacking, it will take many turns to reach 7 counters, making this a very slow plan. The choice of GPT4om Rookie over other targets is reasonable since they have no blockers.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked GPT4om Rookie with Sylvan Safekeeper for 1 damage and a Beastmaster Ascension counter.
annotations.betterLine: The attack itself is fine for the quest counter, and any of the three opponents without blockers would work equally well. This is a marginal decision at best.

annotations.description: Cast Timberwatch Elf (a 1/2 that gives +1/+1 with only itself as an Elf) without first playing a land, when playing Forest first would have enabled casting Soul of the Harvest (6/6 trample + card draw engine) or Siege Behemoth (7/4 hexproof). Timberwatch Elf is extremely low impact with no board presence.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Timberwatch Elf without playing a land first, using only 3 of 6 available mana
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest first (7 mana available), then cast Soul of the Harvest (6 mana) for a 6/6 trampler with a powerful card draw ability, or Siege Behemoth (7 mana) for a 7/4 hexproof creature. Either represents a far more impactful board presence.

annotations.description: Blood Artist's 1 damage was directed at Kimi25 Story who is at 41 life (the highest life total), when GPT4om Rookie is at only 15 life and would be a much more impactful target for incremental damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Kimi25 Story (41 life) with Blood Artist's drain trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Target GPT4om Rookie (15 life) with the Blood Artist trigger to apply pressure to the most vulnerable player.

annotations.description: With 7 mana available (and Gargoyle Castle as an unplayed land drop for 8 total), Kimi25 Story cast a 1/1 Sylvan Ranger instead of deploying a major threat. The reasoning cited Soul of the Harvest triggering, but Soul of the Harvest is in hand, not on the battlefield. The optimal line would be to play Gargoyle Castle first, then cast Soul of the Harvest (6 mana) + Sylvan Ranger (2 mana) to get the 6/6 trampler AND draw a card from it, or at minimum cast Siege Behemoth (7 mana) as a 7/4 hexproof threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sylvan Ranger for 2 mana, wasting 5 mana and deploying only a 1/1
annotations.betterLine: Play Gargoyle Castle as land drop, then cast Soul of the Harvest (6 mana) followed by Sylvan Ranger (2 mana) to get a 6/6 trampler and draw a card from Soul's trigger, or cast Siege Behemoth (7 mana) as a massive hexproof threat

annotations.description: Kimi25 Story has 7 lands (6 Forests + Oran-Rief, the Vastwood) and passed without casting anything. They have several castable spells: Sylvan Ranger (1G), Siege Behemoth (5GG - exactly 7 mana), or Soul of the Harvest (4GG - 6 mana). Soul of the Harvest would provide card draw for future creatures, and Siege Behemoth is a powerful 7/4 with hexproof. They also have Gargoyle Castle which could be played as a land drop if they haven't made one yet. Instead they passed and had to discard down to 7, losing a card for nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells, then had to discard a card due to hand size limit (8 cards in hand, maximum 7).
annotations.betterLine: Cast Soul of the Harvest (4GG = 6 mana) to establish a card draw engine and reduce hand size naturally, or cast Siege Behemoth (5GG = 7 mana) as a massive hexproof threat. Either play would have used available mana productively and avoided the forced discard.

annotations.description: Discarded Soul of the Harvest based on the false belief it was already on the battlefield (it was not). Soul of the Harvest would have been valuable with a hand full of creatures (Sylvan Ranger, Masked Admirers, Siege Behemoth, Terastodon) to trigger its card draw ability. The reasoning was factually wrong about the game state.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Soul of the Harvest, believing it was already on the battlefield
annotations.betterLine: Discard Grim Flowering instead - it's a one-shot draw spell that competes at 6 mana, whereas Soul of the Harvest provides ongoing card advantage with the multiple creatures in hand. Alternatively, Wave of Vitriol could be discarded as more situational.

annotations.description: Kimi25 Story has 6 mana available (5 Forests + Oran-Rief) and passed without casting anything. Sylvan Ranger costs only 1G and would fetch a basic land, helping ramp toward the expensive spells in hand (Terastodon, Wave of Vitriol, Siege Behemoth). It also triggers Beastmaster Ascension on future attacks and puts a body on the board. Additionally, they have 8 cards in hand and will need to discard to hand size, so casting Sylvan Ranger would avoid wasting a card to discard. Instead, they passed and discarded a card for no benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells, then had to discard down to 7 cards.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sylvan Ranger (1G) to search for a basic land, putting a body on the board and avoiding the forced discard. Could also play Gargoyle Castle or Haunted Fengraf as their land drop if they hadn't already, and potentially cast Masked Admirers (2GG) to draw a card and develop the board.

annotations.description: Discarded Sylvan Ranger instead of Masked Admirers. Masked Admirers has a built-in ability to return from graveyard to hand whenever you cast a creature spell (for {G}{G}), making it the ideal discard since you can recover it later. Sylvan Ranger's land-fetching ETB, while less impactful at 7 lands, still has more 'lost value' when discarded since it cannot be recurred.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Sylvan Ranger
annotations.betterLine: Discard Masked Admirers, which can be returned from graveyard to hand by paying {G}{G} when casting any creature spell, effectively making the discard free.

annotations.description: Kimi25 Story passed with 6 untapped mana and Grim Flowering in hand, which would draw 7 cards (7 creature cards in graveyard). They have zero creatures on board and need to rebuild. Even Elvish Visionary or Masked Admirers would have been productive plays. Passing here wastes an entire turn's worth of mana with powerful options available.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the turn without casting any spells, leaving 6 mana unused.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Grim Flowering (5G) to draw 7 cards from the 7 creature cards in graveyard, massively refueling their hand. Could also play Gargoyle Castle or Haunted Fengraf as a land drop first.

annotations.description: Cast Terastodon before playing a land for the turn. Also, the reasoning references 'Soul of the Harvest triggers' but Soul of the Harvest is in the graveyard, not on the battlefield. The land drop should come first as it's free mana/value that could matter later.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Terastodon without first playing a land from hand (Forest, Gargoyle Castle, or Haunted Fengraf were available)
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (Forest for immediate green mana, or Haunted Fengraf/Gargoyle Castle for utility), then cast Terastodon. The extra land could be relevant for future turns or activating abilities.

annotations.description: Kimi25 Story selected their own Beastmaster Ascension as a target for removal/bounce, destroying a key piece of their own win condition that they've been building quest counters on. There were opponent permanents available to target instead.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected their own Beastmaster Ascension as one of the noncreature permanent targets
annotations.betterLine: Target opponents' permanents like Prismari Campus or other enemy-controlled noncreature permanents instead of their own enchantment
